# Exact face isolation and a limitation of atomic fiber representatives

This note keeps three statements separate: an exact identity for full
mixed depth on exposed base faces, a strict obstruction to a one-point
atomic certificate even after optimizing all representatives, and the
larger actual depth of the same example. It is not an obstruction to
selecting a genuine best center of an actual anchored-face mixed body.

## 1. Exact raw depth on every exposed base face

Let P be a finite integer base set, let K_z be compact fibers, and give
their disjoint union S any finite Borel measure mu supported on those
fibers. This includes the actual intrinsic Hausdorff measure in the task.
For any point y define raw depth as the infimum of mu(H) over all closed
ambient halfspaces H containing y. Write D_S for this depth. For a face
F of Q=conv(P), let S_F be the union of fibers with bases in F, with the
RESTRICTION of the original measure.

For every y in S_F,

    D_S(y)=D_{S_F}(y).                                   (1)

One inequality follows because mu restricted to S_F is at most mu.
For the reverse, expose F by a base affine functional l with l=0 on F
and l<0 on P outside F. Given any ambient halfspace H={L>=b} containing
y, replace it by H_N={L+N l>=b}. On every fiber over F this has exactly
the same closed trace as H. Compactness bounds L on each of the finitely
many other fibers, and -l has a positive minimum there. Thus a finite
N excludes all these fibers. The new normal is nonzero for all but at
most one choice of N, which can be avoided. Consequently

    mu(S intersect H_N)=mu(S_F intersect H).

Taking infima proves (1), without assuming an attaining cap or removing
boundary mass. The full face Q makes the assertion immediate.

Every base lies in the relative interior of its minimal face, so the
inclusion-maximal integer-anchored faces cover P. Therefore

    sup_(y in S) D_S(y)
      =max_(maximal anchored F) sup_(y in S_F) D_{S_F}(y). (2)

If y lies above F intersect G, (1) applied also to that intersection
gives D_{S_F}(y)=D_{S_G}(y)=D_{S_(F intersect G)}(y). This retains shared
boundary fibers exactly; their contribution is not duplicated.

In particular, a universal lower bound Gamma_d mu(S)/2^n for the right
side of (2) is already the full OC assertion on this class of bases.
Face isolation does not supply that mass bound by itself.

## 2. An actual six-fiber example

Let Q=conv{(0,0),(2,0),(0,2)} and P=Q intersect Z^2. Its three vertices
will be called v_i and its three edge midpoints m_ij. Put

    K_(v_i)=[0,1/2],       K_(m_ij)=[0,1],
    C=conv union_(z in P) ({z} times K_z).                 (3)

These are exactly the integer fibers of C. At a vertex only that
fiber can contribute. A midpoint can use only its own edge, and the
Minkowski average of its two endpoint fibers is [0,1/2], contained in
its prescribed [0,1]. There are no other integer bases. Thus C is a
full convex body in R^3, C=conv(S), and

    M=9/2,    max |K_z|=1 < M/4=9/8.                     (4)

All four parities occur: the three vertices have parity (0,0), and the
three midpoints have the three other parities. The maximal anchored
faces are precisely the three edges, each having fiber mass 2 and two
occupied parities.

The coarse certificate Gamma_1 mass/occupied-parity-count of an edge
is 1/2. Even allowing arbitrary actual convex subpieces on these edges
cannot increase this individual certificate: a subpiece with one
positive fiber has mass at most 1; a subpiece with at least two positive
fibers occupies both edge parities and has mass at most 2. If both
endpoint fibers have positive lengths, their midpoint fiber necessarily
has positive length by convexity, so an apparent one-parity exception
does not occur. This is only a limitation of that scalar certificate.

## 3. Optimizing every representative and its actual own-depth weight

A stronger valid certificate selects an arbitrary x_z in K_z in every
fiber and assigns its actual ordinary raw depth

    t_z=min(x_z,b_z-x_z),
    b_z=1/2 at a vertex and b_z=1 at a midpoint.

Let nu_x=sum_z t_z delta_(z,x_z). Every closed ambient halfspace H
satisfies

    mu(S intersect H) >= nu_x(H),                         (5)

because each captured representative certifies at least t_z of its
own fiber; a pure integer cap captures the whole relevant fiber. Hence
the exact atomic depth of any selected graph point is a legitimate
lower certificate for its true mixed depth. No affine compatibility or
generic position of this selected graph is assumed.

For the actual body (3), the best possible such certificate is exactly

    sup_(all selections x) max_z D_(nu_x)(z,x_z)=1/2.     (6)

To prove the upper bound, a base vertex can be isolated by a pure base
normal, so its graph depth is t_z<=1/4. At an edge midpoint, first
isolate its base edge as in Section 1, retaining the three selected
points on that edge. If these are not collinear, the midpoint graph
point is a vertex of their triangle and can be isolated, giving depth
t_0<=1/2. If they are collinear, parameterize the edge bases as -1,0,1.
Then x_0=(x_-+x_+)/2 with x_-,x_+ in [0,1/2]. In particular x_0<=1/2,
so t_0=x_0. The exact atomic depth of the middle of three collinear
points is t_0+min(t_-,t_+). Since t_±<=1/2-x_±,

    t_0+min(t_-,t_+)
       <=x_0+1/2-max(x_-,x_+) <=1/2.

This treats every selection and every base. For attainment, select the
ordinary centroids, namely x_v=1/4 and x_m=1/2. Each midpoint has own
weight 1/2 and is an exposed graph point after its edge is isolated.
Its atomic depth is therefore exactly 1/2, proving (6).

The OC raw target in this example is

    (Gamma_1/4) M = 9/16 > 1/2.                           (7)

Thus even optimization of all representatives, all their exact ordinary
depth weights, and all atomic halfspaces cannot prove the target here.
This is stronger than merely fixing the actual centroid graph. It is
also distinct from the archived compatible-selector summed-budget
obstruction: the present certificate optimizes exact graph depth and
does not impose compatibility on the chosen representatives.

## 4. The exact full mixed depth repairs the atomic loss

On each anchored edge the actual intervals, in base coordinates -1,0,1,
are [0,1/2],[0,1],[0,1/2]. At an endpoint base the largest raw depth is
1/4, by exact isolation and the ordinary interval formula.

At the middle point (0,x), 0<=x<=1, a halfspace with positive continuous
normal has the form X>=x+t z. The own-fiber contribution is 1-x. If
f(s)=min(1/2,max(1/2-s,0)), the endpoint contribution has exact infimum

    inf_t [f(x-t)+f(x+t)]
       =min(1/2,max(1-2x,0)).                             (8)

For 0<=x<=1/4 it equals 1/2, attained by taking one endpoint full and
one empty. For 1/4<=x<=1/2 it equals 1-2x, attained when both thresholds
are proper, for example t=0. For x>=1/2 it is zero at t=0. A direct
lower bound follows by considering whether both thresholds lie in
[0,1/2], one lies below 0, or one lies above 1/2; these alternatives
give respectively 1-2x, at least 1/2, or at least (1-2x)_+.

For negative continuous normal, reflect thresholds in 1/4, or perform
the same calculation with g(s)=min(1/2,max(s,0)). The exact endpoint
infimum is min(2x,1/2), so the total is x+min(2x,1/2). Pure integer
halfspaces through the middle capture its entire interval and at least
one endpoint interval, with mass at least 3/2. Consequently the full
raw depth is exactly

    D(x)=min{1-x+min(1/2,(1-2x)_+), x+min(2x,1/2)}.      (9)

On [0,1/4] it is at most 3/4; on [1/2,1] it is at most 1/2. In the
remaining interval it is min(2-3x,x+1/2), which has its unique maximum
at x=3/8, of value 7/8. By (2), the original six-fiber body therefore
has exact global raw maximum 7/8 and normalized maximum

    (7/8)/(9/2)=7/36 > 1/8=Gamma_1/4.                   (10)

All normal directions and closed boundary traces are included in
(8)-(9); interval endpoints have zero H_1-mass. This actual center uses
continuous tail mass that the representative-only certificate (5)
ignores. There is no obstruction here to full anchored-face selection.
